Summary: Command to status value feedback operation for double indexed descriptions having hex representation.
Preconditions:
1. Use “0_sta j 2 sf_CommandFeedback_PGE_13-Bit Configuration_ForTesting.csv” as the exchange CSV configuration.
2. Set the bits per MCD to 16 from tools->Properties->Point tab.
3. For a MCD point, assign the description as [10bx:10ax].
Actions:
1. Open ASE2000 in RTU mode.
2. Select PGE protocol in exchange mode and import the configuration CSV file. Set the bits per MCD to 16 from tools->Properties->Point tab.
3. Start RTU.
4. Open ASE2000 in Master mode and repeat Step 2.
5. Issue Basic MCD having RTU ID as 40 and LUN address 1.
6. Issue Open Select/Close Select having sequence number 0bx, RTU ID 40 and LUN address 1.
7. Then issue pulse having RTU ID 40.
8. Issue Basic MCD having RTU ID as 40 and LUN address 1.
Expected Results:
1. Confirm whether the control operations sequence is displayed in line monitor.
2. Confirm whether the value of MCD point with description [10bx:10ax] in the Point List on the RTU side updates to 0-0 after completing step 7.
3. Confirm the Point List values on the RTU side are reflected on the Master side after completing step 8.

Summary: Performing File Write and Read operation without increment values for configured points.
Preconditions:
1. The common address utilized should be the one used for configuring points. For example, if the common address "10" was used for configuring points of type Single Point, then same common address "10" must be used during read operations.
2. Set Information Address with the value used during write operation, say 123.
3. Set Name of file as Transparent.
Actions:
1. Open ASE2000 in Task mode.
2. Select ‘Edit’ > ‘Configure RTUs...' to open ‘Configure RTUs Wizard’ page.
3. On the line marked *, provide the device Name, Id and select IEC104 protocol from the Protocol drop-down list. Proceed by clicking 'Next'.
4. Select Point Type as Single-Point, Measurand Normalized, Measurand scaled and Integrated Totals. Enter ‘First Point Id’, and ‘Point Count’ say 5 for each of this point in point configuration display along with Common address, say 10. Click the ‘Finish’ button to exit the Configure RTUs Wizard.
5. Switch to RTU Simulation Mode and start RTU.
6. Open another instance of ASE2000 in task mode. By default this instance will open in Master Simulation mode else switch to this simulation mode.
7. Verify that the selected device matches the one configured in RTU mode. If not, repeat step 2, check the 'Display' checkbox for the desired device, and then select 'Finish'.
8. Click on Connect Button to establish connection between the master and slave. Select Initialization > Start DT and use ‘Send Once’ to send initialization request.
9. Read general interrogation, counter interrogation and read command using ‘Send Once’ button.
10.Select File Operations > Write file.
i. Set Common Address to match the initial common address value used for point configuration,(say 10).
ii. Set Information address (Eg. 123).
iii. Select local file with some content and set Name of file as Transparent.
iv. Use ‘Send Once’ to verify that it works
11.Select Read file
i. Set Common Address, Information address and Name of file to match those used in write operation, say 10, 123 and Transparent respectively
ii. Select a local file path and set file name to create a new file.
iii. Use ‘Send Once’ to verify that it works
Expected Results:
1. Check the request and response messages in Line monitor and Messages tab.
2. Verify after completion of read or write operation, master is sending “last section/segment” as second last request which on treenode expansion show “section transfer without deactivation (Last Segment)” under ASDU subnode.
3. Verify after completion of read or write operation, master is sending “last section/segment” as last request which on treenode expansion show "file transfer without deactivation (Last Section)" under ASDU subnode.
4. Verify the file is created with the contents in the specified location after read operation.
Remarks: Case applicable only for file upto size 498kb.

Summary: Performing File Write and Read operation with increment values for configured points in balanced transmission mode.
Preconditions:
1. Connect BCOM-USB. Make proper connections neseccerry for loopback connection.
2. Check whether balanced mode is enabled.
3. The common address utilized should be the one used for configuring points. For example, if the common address "10" was used for configuring points of type Single Point, then same common address "10" must be used during read operations.
4. Set Information Address with the value used during write operation, say 123.
5. Set Name of file as Transparent.
Actions:
1. Open ASE2000 in Task mode.
2. Select ‘Edit’ > ‘Configure RTUs...' to open ‘Configure RTUs Wizard’ page.
3. On the line marked *, provide the device Name, Id and select IEC101 protocol from the Protocol drop-down list. Proceed by clicking 'Next'.
4. Select Point Type as Single-Point and Measurand scaled. Enter ‘First Point Id’, and ‘Point Count’ say 5 for each of this point in point configuration display along with Common address, say 10. Click the ‘Finish’ button to exit the Configure RTUs Wizard.
5. Select 'Tools' > 'Properties' to open 'Properties' page. Now select 'IEC 60870-5-101' > 'Options' check the 'Enabled' checkbox displayed in 'Balanced Mode Options' area and click 'OK'.
6. Assign increment values to the points in the PointList tab. Switch to RTU Simulation Mode and start RTU.
7. Open another instance of ASE2000 in task mode. If not already in Master Simulation mode, switch to this. Verify that the selected device matches the one configured in RTU mode. If not, repeat step 2, check the 'Display' checkbox for the desired device, and then select 'Finish'.
8. Click on Connect Button to establish connection between the master and slave. Select Initialization > Link Status & Rest Link and use ‘Send Once’ to send initialization request.
9. Read general interrogation, counter interrogation and read command using ‘Send Once’ button.
10.Select File Operations > Write file.
i. Set Common Address to match the initial value used for point configuration,(say 10).
ii. Specify Information address (Eg. 123).
iii. Select a local file with content and set Name of file as ‘Transparent’.
iv. Use ‘Send Once’ to verify functionality.
11.Select Read file
i. Set Common Address, Information address and Name of file to match those used in write operation (say 10, 123 and Transparent respectively).
ii. Choose a local file path and specify a new file name.
iii. Use ‘Send Once’ to verify functionality.
Expected Results:
1. Check the request and response messages in Line monitor and Messages tab.
2. Verify increment operation after step 9.
3. Verify the file is created with the contents in the specified location after read operation.
Remarks: Case applicable only for file upto size 498kb. Need to wait for amble amount of time until the read operation completes.

Summary: Step command to analog translation operation for single indexed descriptions with decimal increment value.
Preconditions:
1. Import a DNP3 LAN-WAN exchange csv configuration file with necessery descriptions added.
2. For a AI point, assign the description as [DOAI:0ax:2].
3. Set Transmit flag for the Analog Input exchange.
4. Disable UDP listen by checking 'Disable UDP Listen' in 'Simulation' subtab under 'DNP3 LAN/WAN' tab.
5. Add 'Dest' value in 'Class 1/2/3/0 Data' to where control comand is to be executed. For ex: if 'Direct Operate Relay' has 'Dest' as 1, then set 'Dest' as 1 for 'Class 1/2/3/0 Data'.
Actions:
1. Open ASE2000 in exchange mode with protocol selected as DNP3 LAN/WAN. Import the configuration CSV file.
2. Select 'Tools' > 'Properties' to open Properties window. Under the 'DNP3 LAN/WAN' tab:
[i]. In 'Simulation' subtab, check 'Disable UDP Listen'.
[ii]. In 'Options' subtab, input host and port. Click OK.
3. Switch to RTU mode of simulation.Start RTU.
4. Repeat Step 1 and 2. If not in Master simulation mode , switch to it. Change 'Dest' value of 'Class 1/2/3/0 Data' to the RTU Id where control comand is executed. For ex: if 'Direct Operate Relay' has 'Dest' as 1, then set 'Dest' as 1 for 'Class 1/2/3/0 Data'.
5. Issue Analog Input with 'Dest' as 1.
6. Edit the exchange object properties: type, value and point index of Direct Operate Relay as Latching relay, Latch off and 10 respectively. Click OK and issue Direct Operate Relay with 'Dest' as 1.
7. Issue Class 1/2/3/0 Data with 'Dest' as 1.
Expected Results:
1. Confirm whether the value of AI point with description [DOAI:0ax:2] in the Point List on the RTU side decrements by 2 after completing step 6.
2. Confirm the Point List values on the RTU side are reflected on the Master side after completing step 7.

2. For a AI point, assign the description as [DOAI:0bx:!12:10].
3. Set Transmit flag for the Analog Input exchange.
4. Disable UDP listen by checking 'Disable UDP Listen' in 'Simulation' subtab under 'DNP3 LAN/WAN' tab.
5. Add 'Dest' value in 'Class 1/2/3/0 Data' to where control comand is to be executed. For ex: if 'Direct Operate Relay' has 'Dest' as 1, then set 'Dest' as 1 for 'Class 1/2/3/0 Data'.
Actions:
1. Load the a2k generated using commandline arguments. (For steps refer the attached document in the remarks).
2. Select 'Tools' > 'Properties' to open Properties window. Under the 'DNP3 LAN/WAN' tab:
[i]. In 'Simulation' subtab, check 'Disable UDP Listen'.
[ii]. In 'Options' subtab, input host and port. Click OK.
3. Switch to RTU mode of simulation.Start RTU.
4. Repeat Step 1 and 2. If not in Master simulation mode , switch to it. Change 'Dest' value of 'Class 1/2/3/0 Data' to the RTU Id where control comand is executed. For ex: if 'Direct Operate Relay' has 'Dest' as 1, then set 'Dest' as 1 for 'Class 1/2/3/0 Data'.
5. Issue Analog Input with 'Dest' as 1.
6. Edit the Direct Operate Relay exchange object properties: qualifier as One point, value as Close and point index as 12. Click OK and issue Direct Operate Relay with 'Dest' as 1.
7. Issue Class 1/2/3/0 Data with 'Dest' as 1.
Expected Results:
1. Confirm whether the value of AI point with description [DOAI:0bx:!12:10] in the Point List on the RTU side have no change after completing step 6.
2. Confirm the Point List values on the RTU side are reflected on the Master side after completing step 7.
Remarks: ASE2K_CommandLineRunningSteps.txt

Preconditions:
Have Valid IP in Tools->Properties.
Ensure SunSpec Simulator is running.
Ensure Device ID is set as 1.

Expected Results: Verify that the exchanges in the exchange list even if inside the exchange has "*" in its Device ID and Trans ID fields, it fetches the Global Device ID and Trans ID from Tools->Properties and sends it appropriately.

1. Open ASE2000 in SunSpec Modbus TCP.
2. Send RML exchange.
3. Send RMPL exchange.
4. Open RMP exchange.
5. Select a model from Model Name dropdown list.
6. Select a datapoint from Name dropdown list. Can be a single datapoint or GRP. Can also select multiple datapoints in the exchange.
7. Observe the line monitor for all datapoints which does not contain any unit, the unit must not be displayed and the value must be only displayed in Line monitor and Messages tab.
8. Example: in Model 701, points [701:0].Grid Connection State and [701:0].Throttle Source Information
Expected Results:
Verify that for datapoints which does contain any unit the value is only displayed in Line Monitor and Messages tab for RMP exchange.
Remarks: We can check if datapoint has unit or not by opening the Object properties of that datapoint and checking if 'Unit' row is present. If it is not present that means it does not contain unit.

Summary: Write a single datapoint in object to the simulator using multiple register write function code(0x10)
Preconditions:
1. Open SunSpec Modbus Simulator exe containing folder in command prompt and use command, modKSim.exe -p 8081 -d 1 to run application. Open a browser and enter "http://localhost:8081/modbus/login" to view UI of simulator. In login page configure Modbus Server Port as 502 and click Submit.
2. Make sure simulator has model 63001
Actions:
1. Open ASE2000 application in exchange mode with protocol selected as "SunSpec Modbus TCP". In Tools => Properties => SunSpec Modbus TCP tab, add IP as 127.0.0.1 and Port as 502.
2. Open exchange properties of RML and RMPL exchange, provide device id as 1. Click Ok. Use Send once button to issue RML exchange then RMPL exchange.
3. Open Write datapoint exchange, select model as 63001. Select object as int16_4. Modify value to another value within the range. Use Send once button to issue the exchange
Expected Results:
1. Verify that request function code is 16(0x10)
2. Verify that write is succesfull by checking the response function code which will be 16(0x10)
3. Verify the request and response frames are as expected and displayed properly in line monitor, messages and object properties

1. Open SunSpec Modbus Simulator exe containing folder in command prompt and use command, modKSim.exe -p 8081 -d 1 to run application. Open a browser and enter
"http://localhost:8081/modbus/login" to view UI of simulator. In login page configure Modbus Server Port as 502 and click Submit.
Actions:
1. Open ASE2000 application in exchange mode with protocol selected as "SunSpec Modbus TCP". In Tools => Properties => SunSpec Modbus TCP tab, add IP as 127.0.0.1 and Port as 502.
2. Open exchange properties of RML and RMPL exchange, provide device id as 1 and Click Ok.
3.Use Send once button to issue RML exchange then RMPL exchange.
4. Open the WDP exchange and select a model which has writable points.
5. Under the Name column, select any datapoint from the dropdown list.
6. Save the file and re-open the file
7. Open the WDP exchange and select new datapoints from the dropdown list of already selected model
Expected Results: Verify that the user is able to successfully add any datapoint under the Name column dropdown list in the object list within the WDP exchange.

Summary: To check if the RTU sends an Authentication Error after an Unsolicited Response when Confirm is selected as Critical, and Aggressive Mode is disabled.
Preconditions:
Have two instances of ASE 2000 – Master and RTU,
Running and connected in Task Mode with the following configuration:
Protocol: DNP3 LAN/WAN
Points: Binary Input / Analog Input points
Property Configuration:
On the Master and RTU Instances:
1. Tools -> Properties -> DNP3 LAN/WAN -> Secure Auth. V5
2. Enable Secure Authentication V5
3. Select any Key Change Method, any (net) MAC Algorithm, any Key Wrap Algorithm. If Symmetric/Asymmetric methods chosen, do the further required configurations. Make sure both instances have the same configuration.
4. Opt. Critical Functions -> Select ‘Confirm’
On the Master Instance:
1. Tools -> Properties -> DNP3 LAN/WAN -> Simulation
2. Check the ‘Disable UDP Listen’
On the RTU Instance:
1. Tools -> Properties -> DNP3 LAN/WAN -> Simulation
2. Check the ‘Enable Unsolicited’
Actions:
1. Send Once: Initialization -> Link Status & Reset Link
2. Send Once: Secure Authentication -> Session Key Change
3. Send Once: Initialization ->Enable Unsolicited Responses
4. On the Master: Point List -> Change the Raw Value of any point
Expected Results: After changing the Raw value of a point on the RTU, a ‘Binary/Analog Input Change Response from RTU’ must be sent from the RTU depending on the point type. On expanding this message in the Messages View, we must have a ‘Binary/Analog Input Change’ group type and a ‘Authentication’ group type. This response from the RTU must not be followed by an ‘Authentication Error Request’ by the RTU.

1. Enable TLS1.3 must be checked in both Master and RTU
2. Use wireshark to capture packets.
Actions:
1. Run ASE2000 RTU in task mode using IEC104 protocol with TLS1.3 configuration
2. Open another ASE2000 task mode instance as master using IEC104 protocol with TLS1.3 configuration.
3. Use Connect button to establish a connection.
Expected Results:
1. Verify that client and server is connected using TLS1.3 and proper handshake take place using Wireshark.
2. Verify tls handshake complete message.

Summary: Switching from Exchange mode to Task mode, the IP address GUI element should not be replaced by the serial COM port exchange element
Preconditions: Open ASE2000 - DNP3 LAN/WAN
Actions:
1) Start ASE2000 in Task mode, RTU simulation
2) Create an RTU definition with network protocol DNP3LAN/WAN
3) Start RTU simulation
4) Start another ASE2000 instance in Task mode, Master simulation
5) Use the same RTU definition as RTU simulation, disable UDP listen for TCP loopback testing
6) Enter loopback IP address (127.0.0.1) and connect
7) Send Link Status & Reset Link command to verify connection
8) Stop connection, switch Master simulation to Exchange mode
9) Switch Master simulation back to Task mode
10) Re-enter loopback IP and attempt to connect
11) Connection should be established
Expected Results:
Confirm that while switching from Exchange mode to Task mode, the IP address GUI element is not replaced by the serial COM port exchange element
Remarks: Check with other LAN protocols

Summary: Try ASE2000 self-signed certificates with Enabled CRL Check for TLS 1.2
Preconditions:
1. Open two instances of ASE2000 in IEC104. (One in RTU mode and one in Master mode)
2. Go to Tools->Properties->IEC104->TLS 1.2
3. Set proper IP and Port number in both instances.
Actions:
1. Enable the Enable CRL Check checkbox.
2. Import/Generate ASE2000 self-signed server certificates in RTU mode.
3. Import/Generate ASE2000 self-signed client certificates in Master mode.
4. Run the RTU.
5. Click on the connect button in Client.
6. Verify that the connection has been established and TLS 1.2 handshake successful message is seen in Line monitor.
Expected Results: Verify that you can successfully establish a TLS connection using ASE2000 self-signed certificates with CRL Check enabled in TLS 1.2

Summary: After selecting Device Attributes object in the Object list, click on the new row below it. And then click on Object properties. Clicking on the new/blank row again will cause a crash.
Actions:
1. Open ASE2000. Set the Protocol as DNP3 LAN/WAN. Go to Exchange mode.
2. From the Exchange List, double-click any exchange to open its properties.
3. Under the Application Layer, click on any row to select the object type.
4. Choose Device Attribute from the dropdown — it will populate the first row, and a second row will appear.
5. Click on the second row — Device Attribute appears by default.
6. Click Object Properties to open its configuration window. Close the Object Properties window.
7. Now, observe that the second row becomes blank. Try clicking on the blank second row.
Expected Results: ASE2000 should not crash when clicking on the new blank row after clicking object properties of newly manually created default Device Attribute object.

Summary: To check if an Event occurs when a DI changes from a non-alarm state to an alarm state
Preconditions:
Have two intances of ASE2000 connected and running for DNP3 LAN WAN, with a few DI, Di2, Analog, points configured, with the following configurations and steps:
MASTER:
1. Tools -> Properties -> Events -> Point Value -> Log (Selected), Display (Selected), Audible (Selected)
2. Tools -> Properties -> DNP3 LAN WAN -> Simulation -> Disable UDP Listen Checked
RTU:
1. Tools -> Properties -> Events -> Point Value -> Log (Not Selected), Display (Selected), Audible (Not Selected)
2. Tools -> Properties -> DNP3 LAN WAN -> Simulation -> Enable Unsolicited Checked
3. Double click on Point List -> Select State1 as Alarm State for a DI point
4. Check the 'Event' check box for that point
STEPS:
1. Play the RTU
2. Connect the Master
3. Send Once: Reset Link & Link Status
4. Send Once: Enable Unsolicited Responses
5. Send Once: All Static Data Scan
Actions: Change the Raw of the Event-enabled point from 0 to 1
Expected Results:
An Event must occur, point must enter an Alarm State:
a. Colour of the point must change: The point on RTU must turn text red; The point on Master must turn background red
b. The Event Log Tab must create an entry with the "Point Type - Point Name - Point Value"
c. The Messages Tab must display the Event on RTU (Master also, if Display selected on Master)
d. The Line Montor Tab must display the Event on RTU (Master also, if Display selected on Master)
e. A sound must be output

Summary: To check if an Event occurs when a DI changes from an alarm state to a non-alarm state
Preconditions: Continue from the state of TC 1
Actions: Change the Raw of the Event-enabled point from 1 to 0
Expected Results:
An Event must occur, Point must exit the Alarm State:
a. Colour of the point must change: The point on RTU must turn text black; The point on Master must turn background yellow
b. The Event Log Tab must create an entry with the "Point Type - Point Name - Point Value"
c. The Messages Tab must display the Event on RTU (Master also, if Display selected on Master)
d. The Line Montor Tab must display the Event on RTU (Master also, if Display selected on Master)
e. A sound must be output

Summary: To check Freeze Counters with Acknowledgement
Preconditions: Have two instances of ASE2000 (Master and RTU) Iin Task Mode, configured for DNP3 LAN/WAN with a few Frozen Counters, Binary Counters, Digital Output Status points, Analog Output Status points, running and connected.
Actions:
1. Send Once: Link Status and Reset Link
2. Send Once: Class Poll
3. Send Once: Freeze Counters with No Acknowledgement set to False
Expected Results:
1. A Freeze Request must go with Function 7 (Immeadiate Freeze), Object 20 (Binary Counter)
2. A Freeze Response must be received with Function 129 (Response)
3. A Frozen Counter Request must be sent with Function 1 (read), Object 21 (Frozen Counter)
4. A Frozen Counter Response must be recieved with Function 129 (response), Object 21 (Frozen Counter). It must have the configured PI points.

Summary: Write single datapoint to the simulator using any write function code(0x10 or 0x06) using Send Once, Send Continuos or Start to see if multiple datapoint write implementation caused any issues for single datapoint write.

3. In Tools->Properties->SunSpec Modbus Serial->Use Only Multi-Register Write Function Code can be checked or unchecked.
4. Open Write datapoint exchange, select any model with writable points. Select one datapoint from datapoint dropdown list (If using 0x06 function code select datapoint with datapoint size 1). Modify value to another value within the range inside Object Properties. Use Send once button to issue the exchange.
Expected Results:
1. Verify that request function code is sent with the selected option from Tools->Properties->Use Only Multi-Register Write Function Code setting. 0x10 if checked and 0x06 if unchecked.

3. Verify the request and response frames are as expected and displayed properly in line monitor, messages and object properties.

Summary:

Preconditions: SunSpec Modbus Simulator executable with serial configuration should be running in the system

2. Ensure that the response sent from the simulator is received accurately in ASE2000, with correct function code, byte count, data values and CRC.
Remarks: For read function code will be always 3.

Summary:
SunS' Header response

Expected Results:

Remarks: In ASCII: 0x53 = 'S', 0x75 = 'u', 0x6E = 'n', 0x53 = 'S'. 21365 = Su 28243 = nS

Summary:
Sending an RML Request Once for SunSpec Modbus TCP
Testing the scenario where configuring a 'Read Model List' Exchange and sending a request from the Master once and receiving the corresponding responses from an active RTU for SunSpec Modbus TCP.
Preconditions: Open SunSpec Modbus Simulator exe containing folder in command prompt and use command, modKSim.exe -p 8081 to run application. Open a browser and enter "http://localhost:8081/modbus/login" to view UI of simulator. In login page configure Modbus Server Port as 502 and click Submit.
Actions:
1. Open ASE2000 application in exchange mode. Navigate to File => Select Protocol and from the protocol list, choose "SunSpec Modbus TCP".
2. In Tools => Properties => SunSpec Modbus TCP tab, add IP as 127.0.0.1 and Port as 502.
3. Open exchange properties of Read Model List exchange, provide device id as 1. Click Ok. Use Send Once button to issue that exchange.
Expected Results:
1. The Master must send requests for one model at a time and must get replies from the RTU for the same.
2. It must terminate with END MODEL REACHED.
3. The application state must exit the playing state, i.e., Start, Send Continuous, Once Buttons must be active, Stop Button must be disabled.

Summary: For DNP3 LAN/WAN, DNP3 Serial, Operate Relay, SBO Relay and Direct Operate Relay, check if Output Point Mapping is working as it should.
Preconditions:
1. Open two instances of ASE2000 in Exchange mode (one master and one RTU).
2. Select DNP3 LAN/WAN or DNP3 Serial protocol.
3. Configure Digital Points with Point IDs in RTU.
4. In the Description field of the Point List of a particular point map it to a digital point.
eg: For Digital-to-Digital mapping - In the Description of DI 2, if you put "[1]", then if you send an operate command to point ID 1 its output will be mapped to DI 2 value.
For Digital-to-Analog mapping - In the Description of AI 2, if you put "[DOAI:2:2]", then if you send an operate command to point ID 2, its value will be used to increment/decrement the analog value by times 2.
Actions:
1. Issue Link status and Reset link commands.
2. Issue Operate Relay, SBO Relay or Direct Operate Relay command after configuring it properly by setting a value and assigning proper point index value which is existing in the configured points.
Expected Results: The value corresponding to the Operate command should be reflected to the respective Digital Input point where it is mapped to.

Master Interrogates with COA X,
with a point configured in the RTU with COA *.
Common Address Format = Unstructured.
Preconditions: Have two instances - Master and RTU, of ASE2000 open, in Exchange Mode, for IEC104 protocol.
Actions:
Configure the Master as following:
StartDT | Frequency = 0 | Flags = Display, Transmit
Interrogation | COA = X | Frequency = 0 | Flags = Display, Transmit
--------------------------------------------
Configure the RTU as following:
M_Point A | COA = * | Flags = Display, Interrogation | Any number of IOAs
--------------------------------------------
Start the RTU, Play the Master.
Expected Results:
The requests and responses must follow the following order:
-> StartDT ACT
<- StartDT CON
-> Type ID = 100 | COT = Activation | COA = X
<- Type ID = 100 | COT = Activation Confirmation | COA = X
<- Type ID = t | COT = Interrogated by general interrogation | COA = X | All the IOAs
<- Type ID = 100 | COT = Activation Termination | COA = X
Remarks: Here, X is an integer in the valid range; 1 to 65534. t is the appropriate Type ID corresponding to the type of point configured.

Summary: IEC104 Master-RTU connection using channel configured endpoint (IP/Port), overriding the Master’s global Host/Port.
Actions:
1. Open two instances of ASE2000 - configure one as Master and another as RTU in Exchange Mode with IEC104 protocol.
2. In RTU, configure global host and port as 127.0.0.1 and 2404 respectively. Start the RTU.
3. In Master, configure global host and port with machine IP and 2404 respectively.
4. Configure channel of Startdt Act exchange as "127.0.0.1:2404" and initiate that exchange.
5. Observe the communication.
Expected Results: 1. Verify that Startdt Act request is being send to and Startdt Con is received from 127.0.0.1:2404 (channel config) and not to the global Host (machine ip).

Summary: IEC104 Master uses the channel configured endpoint (IP/Port) to establish IEC 104 communication across two machines, overriding the Master’s global Host/Port.
Preconditions: Require 2 PCs
Actions:
1. Open an ASE2000 instance as RTU in Exchange Mode with IEC104 protocol using machine IP and 2404 as global Host and Port. Start RTU.
2. In another machine, open an ASE2000 instance as Master in Exchange Mode with IEC104 protocol using 127.0.0.1 and 2404 as global Host and Port.
3. In Master, configure channel of Startdt Act exchange as "<RTU Machine IP>:2404" and initiate that exchange.
4. Observe the communication.
Expected Results: 1. Verify that Startdt Act request is being send to and Startdt Con is received from "<RTU Machine IP>:2404" (channel config) and not to the global Host.

Summary: When multiple RTUs exist on different machines, a Master exchange bound to a specific Channel targets only that channel’s endpoint; no traffic is routed to other (global/local) endpoints.
Preconditions: Require 2 PCs
Actions:
1. Open two instances of ASE2000 in Machine1 - configure one as Master and another as RTU in Exchange Mode with IEC104 protocol using machine1 IP and 2404 as global Host and Port. Start RTU.
2. In machine2, open an ASE2000 instance as RTU in Exchange Mode with IEC104 protocol using machine2 IP and 2404 as global Host and Port.
3. In Master instance, configure channel of Startdt Act exchange as "<Machine2 IP>:2404" and initiate that exchange.
4. Observe the communication.
Expected Results:
1. Verify that Startdt Act request is being send to and Startdt Con is received from "<Machine2 IP>:2404" (channel config).
2. Verify that no StartDT traffic is attempted to <Machine1 IP>:2404 for this exchange.

Summary: GI with single ASDU executed by the Master over the channel configured endpoint (IP/Port), overriding the Master’s global Host/Port.
Preconditions: Require 2 PCs
Actions:
1. Open an ASE2000 instance as RTU in Exchange Mode with IEC104 protocol using machine ip and 2404 as global Host and Port.
2. Configure a single asdu, say Single point in rtu with Interrogate flag enabled. Start the RTU.

Summary:
To verify the behaviour of an Interrogation request in IEC104 Exchange Mode where,
Master Interrogates with COA X,
with a point configured in the RTU with COA *.
Common Address Format = Unstructured.
Preconditions: Have two instances - Master and RTU, of ASE2000 open, in Exchange Mode, for IEC104 protocol.
Actions:
Configure the Master as following:
StartDT | Frequency = 0 | Flags = Display, Transmit
Interrogation | COA = X | Frequency = 0 | Flags = Display, Transmit
--------------------------------------------
Configure the RTU as following:
M_Point A | COA = * | Flags = Display, Interrogation | Any number of IOAs
--------------------------------------------
Start the RTU, Play the Master.
Expected Results:
The requests and responses must follow the following order:
-> StartDT ACT
<- StartDT CON
-> Type ID = 100 | COT = Activation | COA = X
<- Type ID = 100 | COT = Activation Confirmation | COA = X
<- Type ID = t | COT = Interrogated by general interrogation | COA = X | All the IOAs
<- Type ID = 100 | COT = Activation Termination | COA = X

Summary: To verify that only the Master sends a TestFR ACT on an idle line when T1, T2, T3 are configured with same values on both Master and RTU in Task Mode
Preconditions: Have two instances of ASE2000 open in Task Mode as Master and RTU configured for IEC104.

1. Open two instances of ASE2000 - configure one as Master and another as RTU in Exchange Mode with IEC101 Terminal Server protocol.
2. Start the RTU active on "127.0.0.1:2404".
3. In Master, configure global host and port as machine IP and 2404 respectively.
4. Configure channel of any Master exchange to 127.0.0.1:2404 and initiate that exchange.
5. Observe the communication.
Expected Results: 1. Verify that TCP connection is initiated to 127.0.0.1:2404 (channel config) and not to the global Host (machine ip).

Summary: To verify that only the RTU sends a TestFR ACT on an idle line when T1, T2, are configured with same values on both Master and RTU, but T3 of RTU is lesser than that of Master in Exchange Mode
Preconditions: Have two instances of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode as Master and RTU configured for IEC104.
Actions:
1. In Tools -> Properties -> IEC104 -> Options of both Master and RTU, enter the same values for T1, T2 (Say, 15, 10). Enter a T3 value in RTU (say, 10) such that it is lesser than that in Master (say, 15).
2. Enable the Transmit flag of StartDT on the Master, make Frequency 0.
3. Start the RTU, Play the Master
4. Wait for the T3 (10 Sec) to elapse
Expected Results: Once the T3 of RTU (10 Sec) is elapsed, only the RTU must send a TestFR ACT to which the Master must respond with a TestFR CON. The same behaviour must be observed at every iteration of T3 elapse.

Summary: To verify TC1, but with Vinci as Master and ASE2000 as RTU
Preconditions:
Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode as RTU. Open an instance of Vinci.
Vinci configuration:
1. Select IEC104 as the protocol
2. Select Master (Client) mode
3. Click on Start
4. Settings: t1 = 15, t2 = 10, t3 = 20
5. Port: 2404
ASE2000 configuration: Same as TC1
Actions:
1. Start ASE2000 RTU, Start Vinci Master
2. Wait for the T3 (10 Sec) to elapse
Expected Results: On Starting of Vinci Master, a StartDT ACT will automatically be sent from Vinci to which ASE2000 must reply with a StartDT CON. Once the T3 is elapsed, only the RTU must send a TestFR ACT to which the Master must respond with a TestFR CON. The same behaviour must be observed at every iteration of T3 elapse.

Summary: Delayed RTU follow-up received after a newer master request becomes active is routed to the current active master
Preconditions:
1. Requires 2 machines - M1 as splitter and RTU; M2 as master

<M1 IP>,40001;40011,<M1 IP>,41001
Actions:
1. Start dummy RTU with delayed response and delayed follow-up on M1 at <M1 IP>:41001 using command :

Expected Results:
